Are there two finite sets of primes $P,Q$ such that\[1=\left(\sum_{p\in P}\frac{1}{p}\right)\left(\sum_{q\in Q}\frac{1}{q}\right)?\]
#307: [ErGr80]
number theory | 
unit fractions
Asked by Barbeau [Ba76]. Can this be done if we drop the requirement that all $p\in P$ are prime and just ask for them to be relatively coprime, and similarly for $Q$?
Cambie has found several examples when this weakened version is true. For example,\[1=\left(1+\frac{1}{5}\right)\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3}\right)\]and\[1=\left(1+\frac{1}{41}\right)\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{7}\right).\]There are no examples known of the weakened coprime version if we insist that $1\not\in P\cup Q$.
It is easy to see that, if $P$ and $Q$ are sets of primes, then $P$ and $Q$ are disjoint, and $\sum_{p\in P\cup Q}\frac{1}{p}\geq 2$, whence $\lvert P\cup Q\rvert \geq 60$.

 As for $(*)$, I don't think you can conclude that the LHS is not divisible by any $q \in Q$. If $P = \{2, 3\}$ and $Q = \{5\}$ then $P$ and $Q$ are disjoint, but they still satisfy $(*)$ while $Q$ is non-empty. In general I advise you to be very wary of proofs generated by AI, and make sure you are familiar with the rules you can find at the top of this page.

 @Dogmachine: that is when considering the weakened coprime condition. 
E.g. 1805 is not prime in $\left(1+ \frac 1{1805} \right)\left(\frac 1{2}+\frac 1{3}+\frac 1{7}+\frac 1{43} \right)=1$.
(P,Q)=([1,3, 11, 331], [2, 5, 1559]) is an example not coming from a primary pseudoperfect number, and showing that the coincidences somewhat may occur
Related versions that also had a positive answer:
i) gcd(p,q)=1 for every $p \in P$ and $q \in Q$
ii) $\gcd\{ p \in P\}=1$ and $\gcd\{ q \in Q\}=1$
If a solution can be found; P determines Q, but for that one has to factorise big numbers. (e.g. taking P to be a set of many small prime numbers different from a few, such that Q can have the other small primes + some large ones that come from the factorisation, gives a computational challenging approach that seems not to be the way to go)
